decisions.rationale: "Prader-Willi" is a disease name used attributively to modify the noun "region" (a chromosomal locus named after the syndrome), so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: "Prader-Willi syndrome" names one specific disease with no further categorization; the whole phrase is preferred over substrings.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Specific Disease; What to Annotate 5: Minimum necessary span

decisions.rationale: "PWS" is the abbreviation of Prader-Willi syndrome, a synonymous mention referring to the same specific disease, annotated as its own mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 6: Synonymous mentions (abbreviation definitions)

decisions.rationale: "complex neurogenetic disorder" describes a family of multiple diseases rather than one specific disease, similar to the "autosomal recessive disease" example.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Disease Class; Examples 10 and 11 (grey-area class terms)

decisions.rationale: "contiguous gene syndrome" refers to a category of syndromes caused by contiguous gene involvement, a family of diseases rather than a single specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Disease Class; Examples 10 and 11

decisions.rationale: "PWS" in "mouse models of PWS" is the disease being modeled, used as a prepositional complement and referring to the specific disease Prader-Willi syndrome.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Specific Disease; What to Annotate 4: Duplicate mentions

decisions.rationale: "PWS" in "aetiology of PWS" refers to the specific disease Prader-Willi syndrome itself, not as an attributive modifier.
"PWS" in "human candidate PWS genes" attributively modifies the noun "genes" and is a disease name used as a modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: "PWS" in "features of PWS" refers to the specific disease Prader-Willi syndrome as the object of "features of".
"PWS" in "molecular basis of PWS" refers to the specific disease Prader-Willi syndrome itself.
"PWS" in the final sentence ("aetiology of PWS and its mouse model") refers to the specific disease Prader-Willi syndrome.
